source.title: Sasan Azadvar, Tenth Protester Hanged Within 42 Days
دادگاه انقلاب شیراز چهار معترض دی را به اعدام محکوم کرد
118th Week of No to Execution Tuesdays Campaign in 56 Prisons Across Iran
xPool Persian latest query for execution, anti-execution, Orumiyeh, Shiraz, and Sasan signals, v36

acquisition.notes: Completed 8 pages, emitted 160 items, stopReason TARGET_ITEMS_REACHED.

claim.statement: Fresh follow-up strengthened the Sasan Azadvar execution signal: HRANA's legal-detail article says his initial death sentence was issued on 26 Esfand 1404, confirmed by the Supreme Court on 7 Ordibehesht 1405, followed by family notification, final visit, execution on 10 Ordibehesht, limited time for retrial efforts, and security restrictions on burial; Iran Human Rights says Azadvar was the tenth protester executed in 42 days since 19 March 2026 and that at least 43 other protesters remained at risk of execution, including two women and three people reportedly under 18 at arrest.
claim.subject: Sasan Azadvar's execution
claim.object: fast-track protester-execution mechanics inside a larger 42-day execution wave

evidence.summary: Existing HRANA source details the sentence, Supreme Court confirmation, final visit, execution, due-process objections, and security-restricted burial.
Iran Human Rights reports Azadvar as the tenth December/January protester executed in 42 days and says at least 43 protesters remain at risk, including two women and three teenagers.

information_depth.rationale: The execution is confirmed by state and rights-side sources; HRANA adds case mechanics and IHRNGO adds wave accounting.

assessment.uncertainty: The precise risk count depends on IHRNGO's case accounting, but the acceleration pattern is independently corroborated.

claim.statement: On 1 May 2026, VOA Persian confirmed that the Shiraz Revolutionary Court sentenced four Dey protest detainees to death: Hamidreza Fathi, Abdolreza Fathi, Saeed Zarei-Kordsholi, and Hamidreza Sabet-Rai; the v36 xPool sample then showed the case being amplified on Persian X, including a high-engagement post by Maryam Moghaddam identifying Judge Mahmoud Sadati as the judge who sentenced Navid Afkari and alleging severe beating/torture in the case.
claim.subject: Shiraz Revolutionary Court
claim.object: four Dey 1404 protest detainees to death, with visible social amplification

evidence.summary: VOA Persian lists Hamidreza Fathi, Abdolreza Fathi, Saeed Zarei-Kordsholi, and Hamidreza Sabet-Rai as four Dey protest detainees sentenced to death by the Shiraz Revolutionary Court.
The xPool sample includes multiple May 1 posts recirculating the four names; Maryam Moghaddam's post tied the case to Judge Mahmoud Sadati and alleged beating/torture.

information_depth.rationale: VOA confirms the case and xPool shows social amplification, but the torture and judge-link details still require court documents or lawyer/family confirmation.

claim.statement: The week-118 No to Execution Tuesdays statement remained a 56-prison hunger-strike signal and sharpened the wartime-repression frame: IranHRM/NCRI report that prisoners condemned the regime's 'war posture', cited recent executions of Amir-Ali Mirjafari, Erfan Kiani, and Amer Ramesh, said two bodies were not returned to families, described beating, torture, forced head-shaving, insults, and legal-rights violations, and called for the UN Fact-Finding Mission to visit Iranian prisons.
claim.subject: No to Execution Tuesdays campaign
claim.object: week 118 hunger strikes across 56 prisons with a wartime-repression statement

evidence.summary: IranHRM carries the full week-118 statement, including the 56-prison list, recent named executions, two bodies withheld, abuse reports, war-posture framing, and UN Fact-Finding Mission appeal.
Existing NCRI source independently reports week 118 across 56 facilities and quotes the statement's wartime-discretion and international-intervention themes.

information_depth.rationale: The prison list and statement details are specific, but the sources are opposition or advocacy aligned and need independent prison-channel corroboration.

claim.statement: A 1-2 May 2026 follow-up found continued urgent alerts, not clean execution confirmation, for the three Orumiyeh death-row prisoners moved to unknown locations: KHRN/IranWire still described Nasser Bakerzadeh, Yaghoub/Karim Yaghoubpour, and Mehrab Abdollahzadeh as transferred and at imminent risk, while the v36 xPool sample recirculated appeals and warnings but did not surface a direct report that any of the three had been executed after the 30 April transfer.
claim.subject: Orumiyeh three execution-risk case
claim.object: urgent transfer/imminent-risk alerts without clean execution confirmation in the v36 sample

evidence.summary: Existing KHRN source reports the 30 April transfers to unknown locations and immediate execution fears.
The xPool result includes urgent Orumiyeh alerts and appeals naming the three prisoners but no clean execution-confirmation cluster.
The notes record that fresh Exa/xPool follow-up found transfer alerts and recirculation, not post-transfer execution confirmation.

information_depth.rationale: This is bounded negative evidence under blackout and rights-reporting delays; it should lower only the probability of already-confirmed execution, not the risk level.

assessment.uncertainty: A prison, family, lawyer, or rights-network update could change this immediately.

claim.statement: The v36 xPool execution sample showed strong Persian X amplification around martyr/family/body themes but not a verified broad in-country action wave: 160 items included high-engagement Sasan Azadvar body and family-grief posts, Orumiyeh execution-risk alerts, Shiraz four death-sentence recirculation, body-withholding/family-repression language, and diaspora/opposition May Day anti-execution posts, but no clean worker, teacher, student, family, or street-action cluster inside Iran beyond prison-campaign and social amplification.
claim.subject: Persian X anti-execution discourse
claim.object: martyr/family amplification without verified broad in-country action crossing

evidence.summary: The xPool query completed 8 pages and emitted 160 items; manual read found Sasan/Orumiyeh/Shiraz/body-family amplification but no clean verified in-country action cluster.
The notes record the high-signal xPool posts and the absence of a clear workplace/student/teacher/street crossing inside Iran.

information_depth.rationale: The dataset is useful for visible discourse topology but cannot observe suppressed channels, private networks, or offline actions.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v36 - executions heat up, broad anti-execution action still unverified
synthesis.summary: The thirty-sixth pass revisits the execution lane. The pressure is not cooling. HRANA's Sasan Azadvar details show a fast track from Supreme Court confirmation on 7 Ordibehesht to execution on 10 Ordibehesht, with little time for retrial efforts and burial restrictions; Iran Human Rights says he was the tenth December/January protester executed in 42 days and that at least 43 protesters remain at risk. The Orumiyeh three remain in the danger zone: KHRN/IranWire describe unknown-location transfers and xPool recirculates urgent appeals, but fresh follow-up did not find clean confirmation that they have been executed after the 30 April transfer. VOA confirms the Shiraz four death-sentence lane, and xPool shows the case being amplified with judge/torture allegations. Prison resistance continues: week 118 of No to Execution Tuesdays is reported across 56 prisons with a war-posture statement, recent named executions, bodies withheld, abuse reports, and a call for UN prison visits. The social reaction is emotionally sharp around Sasan's body, family grief, Orumiyeh alerts, and Shiraz names, but it is still mostly prison/opposition/diaspora/X amplification rather than verified broad worker, student, teacher, family, or street action inside Iran. Net: execution pressure is a live regime-control crack, but the mobilization crossover remains unproven.
synthesis.limitations: xPool is reaction evidence, not verification of offline action. Opposition and advocacy sources are specific but need prison, family, lawyer, court, or official corroboration where possible. The Orumiyeh no-confirmation finding is bounded by blackout conditions and reporting lag.

information_depth.rationale: The synthesis combines existing state/rights rows, fresh IranHR and VOA sources, a fuller prison-campaign statement, and a completed 160-item xPool sample.

operations.rationale: The fast-track execution plus IHRNGO risk count directly updates whether rapid protester executions deter protest or create named martyrs.
The Sasan timeline and 10-in-42-days count directly update whether protester executions are accelerating.
The Orumiyeh three are part of the late-April imminent-risk set; bounded non-confirmation preserves the risk without claiming execution occurred.
The Shiraz four directly update whether late-April and early-May death-sentence cases move toward execution.
The 56-prison hunger strike is the strongest prison-side anti-execution mobilization signal and sets a baseline for whether action crosses outward.
The xPool sample tests whether anti-execution mobilization has crossed into workplace, student, family, or street action inside Iran.

operations.reason: v36 updates the active read from campus control to the time-sensitive execution lane: fresh evidence shows execution pressure heating and visible anti-execution amplification, but no verified broad in-country action crossover yet.
